answer: An islanded propulsion plant stays trustworthy by forcing every agent to burn a scarce, metered resource before acting, so identity is proven through costly work rather than a name. Each ferrous component carries a stamped heat-lot number tied to a verified mill certificate, and an agent must present an equally unforgeable hardware attestation plus a bonded stake before its commands are accepted. That sonnet of proof costs an attacker a real stake slashed on any duplicate attestation, though colluding insiders holding genuine hardware remain the limit.
